tasks.label: Pico: Doctor (check toolchain)
tasks.detail: Verify mpremote, picotool and the MicroPico extension are installed, then list serial ports.

tasks.label: Pico: List serial ports
tasks.detail: Show every serial device mpremote can see. Use this to find your port.

tasks.label: Pico: Install type stubs
tasks.detail: Install the MicroPython RP2040 stubs into typings/ so Pylance resolves machine, utime, ustruct, _thread. Reload the window afterwards.

tasks.label: Pico: Type-check project
tasks.detail: Run pyright over src/ and template_program.py using pyrightconfig.json -- the same analysis Pylance does, but in one shot.

tasks.label: Pico: Install dev dependencies
tasks.detail: pip install mpremote and the MicroPython stubs into your active Python environment.

tasks.label: Pico: REPL
tasks.detail: Attach to the MicroPython prompt without soft-resetting. Ctrl-C stops the running program, Ctrl-] detaches.

tasks.label: Pico: Upload src/ to board
tasks.detail: Thonny's 'upload every file' step: copies src/ onto the Pico root, creating lib/ as needed.

tasks.label: Pico: Upload current file
tasks.detail: Copy just the file in the active editor to the Pico root.

tasks.label: Pico: Run current file (not saved to flash)
tasks.detail: Execute the active editor's file on the board from RAM. Fastest way to try something.

tasks.label: Pico: Mount src/ as board filesystem
tasks.detail: Dev loop with zero flash writes: the Pico imports straight from src/ over USB. Ctrl-] to detach.

tasks.label: Pico: Upload src/ then open REPL
tasks.detail: Sync, hard reset, and attach so you can watch main.py boot. The closest thing to Thonny's green Run button.

tasks.label: Pico: List files on board
tasks.detail: Recursive listing of the Pico filesystem.

tasks.label: Pico: Print a file from board
tasks.detail: cat a file that lives on the Pico (e.g. program.py, calibration.json).

tasks.label: Pico: Print filesystem layout
tasks.detail: Read the board's real flash geometry (block size, block count, free space). Use it to confirm the --fs-base/--fs-size a UF2 build should use.

tasks.label: Pico: Download a file from board
tasks.detail: Pull a file off the Pico into the repo root.

tasks.label: Pico: Stop running program
tasks.detail: Send Ctrl-C to break out of main.py's loop and leave the board at the prompt.

tasks.label: Pico: Reset board
tasks.detail: Hard reset. main.py runs again from the top.

tasks.label: Pico: Soft reset board
tasks.detail: Restart the interpreter without power-cycling (Thonny's 'Send EOF / Soft reboot'). main.py reruns.

tasks.label: Pico: Settle after reset
tasks.detail: Internal step: gives the board a moment to finish rebooting before another task grabs the port.

tasks.label: Pico: Wipe board filesystem
tasks.detail: Delete every user file on the Pico. Prompts for confirmation.

tasks.label: UF2: Check firmware toolchain
tasks.detail: Checks Docker (or a local ARM toolchain) and the MicroPython submodule. Run this first.

tasks.label: UF2: Build release (the file end users update with)
tasks.detail: Compiles custom firmware with main.py/roboxlib.py/etc. frozen in, and writes build/robox-<version>.uf2 -- verified to carry zero filesystem blocks, so config.json/program.py always survive. See docs/RELEASE.md.

tasks.label: UF2: Build release (local toolchain, no Docker)
tasks.detail: Same as above, but compiles with arm-none-eabi-gcc/cmake straight off PATH instead of Docker.

tasks.label: UF2: Inspect a .uf2
tasks.detail: Show a UF2's flash layout and list the files in its filesystem. Works on a build or on a board dump.

tasks.label: UF2: Verify a release is filesystem-safe
tasks.detail: Fails unless the given UF2 has zero blocks in the filesystem region. 'UF2: Build release' already runs this automatically.

tasks.label: UF2: Reboot board into BOOTSEL
tasks.detail: Put the Pico into mass-storage mode so picotool can read its flash. The RPI-RP2 volume appears.

tasks.label: UF2: Save board flash to build/
tasks.detail: picotool save -t uf2. The board must already be in BOOTSEL mode.

tasks.label: UF2: Capture from board (sync -> BOOTSEL -> save)
tasks.detail: The old hardware workflow: upload src/, reboot to BOOTSEL, dump the whole flash to build/*.uf2. Use it to snapshot a board; prefer 'UF2: Build release (the file end users update with)' for releases.
dependsOn: UF2: Save board flash to build/

tasks.label: UF2: Wait for BOOTSEL volume
tasks.detail: Internal step: gives the RPI-RP2 volume a few seconds to mount before picotool runs.
tasks.command: echo 'Waiting for the board to reappear in BOOTSEL mode...' && sleep 4

tasks.label: UF2: Flash a .uf2 onto the board
tasks.detail: Load an existing UF2 onto a Pico that is in BOOTSEL mode.

inputs.description: Path on the Pico (e.g. program.py or lib/picozero/picozero.py)
Path to the .uf2 file to flash
